title: Close the gap

predict.q: Real output is 460; full-employment output is 500. The gap is 40. With lots of spare capacity, the government raises spending by 10. What happens to real output?

options.s: It rises by exactly 10, the amount spent
options.fb: The first 10 becomes income for builders and suppliers, who spend part of it. Output rises by more.

options.s: It rises by more than 10, as the extra income is spent again and again
options.fb: With 0.75 of extra income re-spent, output rises by 10 × 4 = 40: the gap closes.

options.s: It falls, because the government must borrow the money
options.fb: Borrowing has costs, but the spending itself raises AD now, so output rises.

options.s: It stays the same: only the price level rises
options.fb: With lots of spare capacity, firms can raise output; prices rise mainly near full capacity.

task: Move the spending slider and the "share re-spent" slider. Find the rise in spending that closes the gap.

target.do: Set the rise in spending to 10 (share re-spent 0.75), then press Check.

takeaway: Because of the multiplier, a rise in spending smaller than the gap can close it, if prices stay steady.
